z-m-06-05.title: If you stick two triangle pieces together, e become hexagon?
z-m-06-05.topic: Triangles and quadrilaterals: side count of shape made by sticking pieces together
z-m-06-05.goal: Learn say side count of shape from joining two triangles fit differ depending how dem join; find and fix wrong part in Sora reasoning.
z-m-06-05.material: Two paper pieces be right triangles. Dem get same size and shape. The two sides beside right angle na 3cm and 4cm, and longest na 5cm. Right angle na square corner; join two right angles and dem form straight line without bend. Join both pieces exactly along one side, no overlap or gap, to make one shape. Better cut paper and try. Read Sora thought line by line. There are 2 pieces and 2 sides beside the right angle.
z-m-06-05.thinking.0: Examining what happen to joined sides
z-m-06-05.prereq.0: Sides and right angles of triangle, quadrilateral, hexagon (Grade 2)
z-m-06-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose one line in Sora thinking wey no correct.
z-m-06-05.s.s1.hint.0: Separate whether each line talk about before or after sticking.
z-m-06-05.s.s1.hint.1: Picture shape when two pieces join along side, then count outside sides one by one.
z-m-06-05.s.s1.line.1: Na two pieces, so 3+3=6 sides total.
z-m-06-05.s.s1.line.2: When you join them, the two joined sides no show outside.
z-m-06-05.s.s1.line.4: E get 6 sides, so any way you join dem, e become hexagon.
z-m-06-05.s.s1.explain: Lines 4 and 5 wrong. Line 3 say joined sides no show outside, so outside sides na 6 minus those two. Line 4 no reflect that. 6 in line 2 correct as side count before joining. If you choose earlier line, separate whether e talk before or after join.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.prompt: This time join 4cm sides, but flip one piece so two right-angle corners meet at one point. If sides joined in one straight line count as one, what shape result?
z-m-06-05.s.s2.hint.0: Picture what two 3cm sides make where both right-angle corners meet.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.hint.1: Trace outside sides one round and count joined straight-line sides only once.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.r.a: You thought joined sides disappear but miss say two sides in one line count as one side.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.r.b: You consider both that joined sides disappear and sides in one line count once.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.r.c: Looks like you count one extra. Trace outer edge and point each side one by one.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.r.d: You use side count before joining. Check again what happen to joined sides.
z-m-06-05.s.s2.explain: Both joined 4cm sides go inside and no show. Remaining are two 3cm and two 5cm sides. But two right angles meet, so 3cm sides make one straight 6cm side. So result triangle, 3 sides.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.prompt: Tell Sora why 'any way you join, it becomes hexagon' wrong. Use joining method you just saw as example.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.hint.0: You fit use same method to count sides from last step.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.hint.1: Think of one example wey make phrase 'any way' wrong.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You count outside sides one by one in your example?
z-m-06-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You know one example enough to break 'any way' claim?
z-m-06-05.s.s3.model.0: E no always hexagon. Joined sides no show outside, and if you join 4cm sides, e fit become triangle.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.model.1: E depend how you join. Join 5cm sides, get quadrilateral with 4 sides.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.model.2: If you join 5cm sides, e become quadrilateral, so no be hexagon.
z-m-06-05.s.s3.model.3: If you join 4cm sides so both right-angle corners meet, result triangle with 3 sides. So it no become hexagon every time.

z-m-06-02.title: Wetin else we need to know the length of strings wey tie together?
z-m-06-02.topic: Length: total length of tied strings (cm)
z-m-06-02.goal: Know say if you tie string ends by overlapping them, the length no just be their total; talk what information you need to state the exact length and make examples of possible lengths.
z-m-06-02.material: Hajun get string 가 wey long 40cm and string 나 wey long 35cm. E overlap the ends of the two strings small and tie them to make one long string. Dem stretch the string straight to measure the length. Hajun talk, 'Na the two string lengths together, so the tied string na 75cm.' We still no know how many cm the overlapping part be.
z-m-06-02.thinking.0: Judge whether the information dem give enough
z-m-06-02.thinking.2: Make different cases wey meet the conditions
z-m-06-02.prereq.0: Read length in cm and two-digit calculation (Grade 2 level)
z-m-06-02.s.s1.prompt: How we fit look at wetin Hajun talk?
z-m-06-02.s.s1.hint.0: Put string 가 and string 나 apart and look which part dey inside both strings wen dem tie them together.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.hint.1: Think how many times the overlapping part suppose enter the total length.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.o.a: Correct. Two strings dey, so just add the lengths.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.r.a: You add the lengths as dem be, without using the condition say the strings overlap and dem tie them.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.o.b: E longer than 75cm. Tying make the string longer.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.r.b: You think say tying make am longer. Remember wetin happen wen string ends overlap as you tie them.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.o.c: E shorter than 75cm. E reduce by the overlapping length.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.r.c: You notice say the overlapping part dey once inside each string but e enter total length only once.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.o.d: We no fit tell. Na because we no know how thick the strings be.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.r.d: You think say information wey no get anything to do with length dey needed. Work out the information wey really needed.
z-m-06-02.s.s1.explain: We overlap and tie the ends, so the overlapping part dey in both strings. So e shorter than combined 75cm by the overlapping length. To know how much e shorter, we need know the overlapping length.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.prompt: Wetin you need know to decide the exact length of the tied string? Choose everything wey go let you decide the exact length once you know am.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.hint.0: Think one by one whether you fit decide the tied string length once you know each choice.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.hint.1: Look whether there dey one way to work out the length and one way to know the length directly.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.o.b: The time e take to tie the strings
z-m-06-02.s.s2.r.b: Time no tell you the length.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.r.c: If you know the overlapping length, you fit remove that much from the lengths of the two strings.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.o.d: Length of the tied string, stretch straight and measure am
z-m-06-02.s.s2.r.d: If you measure directly, you fit know the total length straight away without calculation.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.explain: If you know the overlapping length, or stretch the tied string straight and measure am directly, you fit know the exact length. One of the two alone enough.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.acc.0: Choosing only the overlapping length fit decide the exact length too. E even better if you also think say you fit stretch am and measure directly.
z-m-06-02.s.s2.acc.1: Choosing only direct measuring method fit tell the exact length too. E even better if you also think say you fit calculate if you know overlapping length.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.prompt: Make we say overlapping length na at least 2cm and at most 7cm (natural number). Make 2 different cases for the possible total length of tied string. Write overlapping length as o and total length of tied string as t (unit cm).
z-m-06-02.s.s3.hint.0: Choose overlapping length and work out how many times that part dey included in the combined length of the two strings.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.hint.1: Write in table how total length change as the overlapping length wey you choose change.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.ok.c1: Overlapping length na natural number from 2cm to 7cm.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.fail.c1: Make overlapping length a natural number from 2 to 7.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.ok.c2: Total length equal combined length of the two strings minus overlapping length.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.fail.c2: Total length no correct. Think again wetin to do with overlapping length from the combined length.
z-m-06-02.s.s3.explain: If overlapping length na 2cm, total na 73cm; if 3cm, na 72cm; and if 7cm, na 68cm. If overlapping length change, total length change too, so plenty possible lengths dey from 68cm to 73cm.
z-m-06-02.s.s4.prompt: How e go good to correct Hajun statement '75cm'? Also write why you correct am that way.
z-m-06-02.s.s4.hint.0: First arrange wetin Hajun talk wey correct and wetin wrong.
z-m-06-02.s.s4.hint.1: Remember the method wey you choose for step above and write wetin to do to state exact length.
z-m-06-02.s.s4.selfAssess.0: You write thinking 'when Hajun statement correct and when e wrong'?
z-m-06-02.s.s4.selfAssess.1: You include wetin you need know to get exact length too?
z-m-06-02.s.s4.model.0: E fit no be 75cm. We overlap and tie the two strings, so e shorter by the overlapping length. If you know how many cm the overlapping part be, subtract am from 75.
z-m-06-02.s.s4.model.1: Stretch the tied string straight and measure am with ruler. One part overlap, so the length go come out shorter than 75cm.

z-m-06-01.title: If hour hand near 5, e mean say na 5 o'clock?
z-m-06-01.topic: Clock: read time with hour hand and minute hand
z-m-06-01.goal: Know say hour hand alone make am hard to decide which hour e be, and say you must read am together with minute hand; then make your own examples of times wey hour hand near 5 but e never reach 5 o'clock.
z-m-06-01.material: Analog clock get hour hand (the hand wey show hour) and minute hand (the one wey show minutes). Wen minute hand point to 12, na exactly the hour, and each number space na 5 minutes. Clock numbers na 1 to 12. Jiho no fit see clock picture directly, and e dey play game to guess time from wetin friend tell am with words. Whether na morning or evening no matter.
z-m-06-01.thinking.0: Delay judgment or add conditions wen information no enough
z-m-06-01.thinking.1: Change your judgment each time new information arrive
z-m-06-01.thinking.2: Make your own examples of cases wey easy to mix up
z-m-06-01.prereq.0: Read on-the-hour and 5-minute times on analog clock (Grade 2 level)
z-m-06-01.s.s1.prompt: Read wetin your friend talk one piece at a time, and each time choose the time wey you fit say now.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.hint.0: Before new information come, first talk in one sentence how certain your judgment be.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.hint.1: Wen new information come, read separately wetin hour hand and minute hand each dey tell.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.info: Your friend talk, 'Hour hand dey very near 5. I no go talk about minute hand yet.'
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.ask: What time you fit say now?
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.after: Hour hand near 5 fit happen just before 5, like 4:50, or just after 5 o'clock. So asking more about minute hand and just guessing 'around 5 o'clock' both okay.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Na 5 o'clock. The number wey hour hand near na 5.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You read the number wey hour hand near as the hour directly. You decide even though you never know minute hand.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.o.b: E fit be around 4 or around 5 o'clock. I need know where minute hand dey.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You consider say hour hand fit dey just before 5 or just after 5.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.o.c: E seem like 5 o'clock but I no fit sure. I go ask more about minute hand.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Na idea to guess with the clues wey you get now, no be to sure, and to try find out more.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Na 4 o'clock. Hour hand never reach 5 yet.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You choose 4 just because e never reach 5. You no consider whether e fit don pass 5 small.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.info: Your friend talk, 'Minute hand point to 10.'
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.ask: Wetin time e be now, in hours and minutes?
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.after: If minute hand point to 10, na 50 minutes. Around 50 minutes, even if hour hand almost touch next number 5, e never reach 5 o'clock, so na 4:50. To talk say na 10 minutes before 5 o'clock na the same time.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Reading minute hand's 10 as 50 minutes correct. But you choose the hour based on number 5 wey hour hand near.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You read number 10 wey minute hand point to as 10 minutes directly. Remember again how many minutes each number space be.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You read the minutes from minute hand and the hour because hour hand never reach 5.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You read the hour as 4, but you read number 10 on minute hand directly as minutes.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.info: Na new problem. Your friend talk, 'This time hour hand don just pass 5, and minute hand point to 2.'
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.ask: What time be this, in hours and minutes?
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.after: Hour hand just pass 5, so na small after 5 o'clock; the 2 for minute hand na 10 minutes. Hour hand show hour and minute hand show minutes.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Reading minute hand's 2 as 10 minutes correct. But you miss say hour hand don already pass 5.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You read the hour from the number hour hand don pass and the minutes from the number minute hand point to, separately.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You read the number 2 for minute hand directly as 2 minutes.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You read number 2 for minute hand as 20 minutes. Check again how many minutes each number space be.
z-m-06-01.s.s1.reflect: At first, from hour hand alone, you fit guess 'around 5 o'clock' or ask more. Wen the new information, minute hand, come, e show say even the hour fit change. You no fit say the number wey hour hand near na the same as the current hour.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.prompt: Make 2 different times wen hour hand nearer to 5 than 4 but e never reach 5 o'clock. Minute hand point exactly to a number (minutes na multiple of 5). Write hour as h and minutes as m. (Example: for 7:15, h=7, m=15)
z-m-06-01.s.s2.hint.0: Choose hour wey no be 5, and choose minutes from multiples of 5.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.hint.1: Make we suppose say for 4:30, hour hand exactly halfway between 4 and 5, then compare how minutes must different to move nearer to 5.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.fail.c1: E must be before 5 o'clock, so set the hour to 4.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.ok.c2: The minute hand point exactly to a number for the minutes.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Set the minutes to multiple of 5 wey be 0 or more but less than 60.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.fail.c3: 4:30 exactly halfway between 4 and 5. To dey nearer to 5, the minutes must pass that point.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.explain: 4:35, 4:40, 4:45, 4:50 and 4:55 all correct examples. 4:30 halfway between 4 and 5, so e no enter under this condition. The more the minutes, the nearer hour hand reach 5, but na only wen minute hand go round full and reach 12, time go be 5 o'clock.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.prompt: Even though hour hand near 5, use one of the times wey you just make as example explain why e no be 5 o'clock.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.hint.0: Talk one of the times wey you choose aloud, then write the number wey minute hand dey on at that time.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.hint.1: Remember where minute hand must dey exactly at 5 o'clock, then compare with current time.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You write exactly the number or minutes wey minute hand point to for your example?
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You write with the idea say 'hour hand near' and 'that hour don reach' different things?
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.model.0: If minute hand point to 10, na 50 minutes. For time to be 5 o'clock, minute hand must go round once more and reach 12, so right now na still 4:50.
z-m-06-01.s.s2.because.model.1: Hour hand dey move small small as time pass and e dey get near 5. But if minute hand never reach 12, like 4:40, na still 4 o'clock.

z-m-06-08.thinking.1: Make different cases wey meet the conditions
z-m-06-08.title: I draw marble 5 times and red show 4 times. Wetin fit dey inside bag?
z-m-06-08.topic: Possibility: guess wetin dey inside bag from the results wey come out
z-m-06-08.goal: From the results, talk different cases wey fit dey inside the bag, and tell difference between 'cases wey fit happen' and 'cases wey more likely'.
z-m-06-08.material: All together, 8 marbles dey inside bag. The marbles na only red and blue. You no fit see inside, so you take out one marble, look the colour, put am back and mix well; you do am 5 times. Result na red 4 times and blue 1 time. Yunha talk, 'Red marbles must plenty pass.' Daon talk, 'Fit be say na only 1 blue marble dey, abi?'
z-m-06-08.thinking.0: Tell apart cases wey fit happen and wey no fit happen
z-m-06-08.thinking.2: Separate wetin certain from wetin na guess

z-m-06-08.s.s1.prompt: Wen this result happen, choose all the ways red and blue marbles fit dey inside bag.

z-m-06-08.s.s1.r.a: You miss say red show once. If red marble no dey at all, you no fit draw one.
z-m-06-08.s.s1.r.b: You notice say even if only 1 red marble dey, e fit show plenty times if person put am back and draw again.
z-m-06-08.s.s1.r.c: You miss say blue show once. If blue marble no dey at all, you no fit draw am.
z-m-06-08.s.s1.r.d: You choose case where both colours dey and red plenty pass.
z-m-06-08.s.s1.explain: Red and blue both show, so both colours must get 1 or more. So both 1 red and 7 blue, and 5 red and 3 blue fit happen. Na only the side wey red plenty pass dey more likely.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different ways the bag fit be and give this result. Write number of red marbles as r and blue as b. All together, 8 marbles dey.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.hint.0: First decide at least how many of each colour must dey inside bag.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.hint.1: Change number of red marbles one by one and write in table how many blue marbles go dey.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.ok.c1: Both red and blue get 1 or more.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.fail.c1: Red and blue both show, so each colour must get 1 or more.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.fail.c2: Red and blue together must be 8.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.explain: All 7 cases fit happen, from 1 red and 7 blue to 7 red and 1 blue. The side wey red plenty pass dey more likely, but the important thing be say no be only one possible case.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.prompt: Compare wetin Yunha talk with wetin Daon talk, then write your own thoughts.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.hint.0: Separate the two things dem talk into wetin you fit know for sure from the result and wetin na guess.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.hint.1: Think separately whether Yunha statement must be correct and whether Daon statement fit happen.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You write separately which case each person dey talk about?
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You tell the difference between 'wetin certain' and 'wetin na guess'?
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.model.0: E seem say red marbles plenty pass, but e no certain. Like Daon talk, only 1 blue marble fit dey, and even if only 1 red marble dey, this kind result fit happen.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.model.1: 4 out of 5 were red, so e make sense to guess say red marbles plenty pass. But blue show too, so e certain say blue marbles dey inside.
z-m-06-08.s.s2.because.model.2: E likely say red marbles plenty pass, but we no fit be sure. This result fit happen even if only 1 red marble dey.

z-m-06-03.title: Where Soyul building-block house plan need correction?

z-m-06-03.material: Unit cube na cube-shaped wooden block wey size na one space. Soyul wan build house shape using all 7 unit cubes. Rules: (1) For floor 1, put unit cubes in one line with no empty space. (2) Floor 2 cubes fit go only directly on top of floor 1 cubes, and only one floor 2 block fit go on each floor 1 block. (3) No build floor 3. Read Soyul plan line by line.

z-m-06-03.thinking.1: Make different ways wey meet the conditions

z-m-06-03.s.s1.hint.1: Count all the places wey floor 2 block fit go on top the 3 floor 1 blocks.

z-m-06-03.s.s2.fail.c3: If floor 2 blocks pass floor 1 blocks, some blocks no go get support.

z-m-06-04.title: Wetin if you measure same hallway twice and length different?
z-m-06-04.topic: Length: values wey differ when dem measure same length several times
z-m-06-04.goal: When repeated measurements of same length differ small, examine measuring method and decide how to state length.
z-m-06-04.material: We measure school hallway with 1m stick. Mark stick end with chalk, place end at mark again and continue. Measure remaining part with cm ruler, write like '3m 40cm'. 1m na 100cm. We no know real hallway length yet.
z-m-06-04.thinking.0: Examining how measurement method affect result
z-m-06-04.thinking.1: Revising judgment as each new value arrive
z-m-06-04.thinking.2: Writing with how much confidence it deserve
z-m-06-04.prereq.0: Know 1m=100cm and read lengths with m and cm (Grade 2)
z-m-06-04.s.s1.prompt: Each time measurement result arrive, choose judgment you fit make now.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.hint.0: When new value come, change both to same unit and compare difference from earlier one.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.hint.1: If values different, first ask how dem measure; check if values measured same way dey close.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.info: Group A measure hallway once and get 3m 40cm.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: How you suppose state hallway length?
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.after: One measurement valuable evidence, but too early to say 'exactly this much.' Suggest measure again, or write 'about'—both okay.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You call one measurement exact length. You never check if repeat give same answer.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Take am as about 3m 40cm and measure once more to check.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You use current value as basis and also think of way to check.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: One measurement no trustworthy, so throw am away.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You throw away useful value. One measurement still valuable evidence.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: By writing 'about,' you leave room say e no exact yet.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.info: Group B measure same hallway again, get 3m 46cm.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: Wetin you think when you see two values (3m 40cm, 3m 46cm)?
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.after: If you subtract 3m 40cm from 3m 46cm, difference na 6cm. E clear say single measurements differ by 6cm. Instead of saying one wrong, ask how dem measure or measure again.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Group A answer correct, Group B wrong.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You no know how dem measure yet, but decide one correct.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Difference na 6cm, but we no fit decide yet which more trustworthy.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You notice gap between values and that no basis to choose yet.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Hallway become longer between both times.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You think hallway length change. Think whether measuring method fit cause difference.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Two values close, so both fit be about 3m 40cm. Measure once more.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You see 6cm gap and consider both approximate length and next action.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.info: It turn out Group A mark stick end with chalk each time, while Group B move stick without marking. Without marking, stick fit overlap or leave gaps easily. Group C mark and measure again, get 3m 41cm.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: How good to summarize hallway length?
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.after: Both marked measurements (3m 40cm, 3m 41cm) differ only 1cm, so that method seem more trustworthy. Still, don't throw away 3m 46cm completely; note 'it may differ because they didn't mark.' You can also state range covering all three values.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Longest, 3m 46cm, na real one; others too short.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You think bigger value always accurate. If stick overlap, answer fit become longer.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Marked values 3m 40cm and 3m 41cm close, so use about 3m 40cm and investigate why 3m 46cm different.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You use closeness of same-method values as basis and investigate reason for other value too.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Each time we measure value differ, so we no fit know hallway length.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You say impossible to know because values differ small. Check whether close values gather around one place.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Trust all three and say hallway between 3m 40cm and 3m 46cm.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You throw away no value and state range they cover.
z-m-06-04.s.s1.reflect: One measurement fit use as 'about' only; second show 6cm difference. When measuring-method information arrive, you get basis for which value more trustworthy. Instead of trusting one as exact, look where values gather and at method together.
z-m-06-04.s.s2.prompt: You wan write hallway length on noticeboard. Write good way and one reason.
z-m-06-04.s.s2.hint.0: Put three measurements side by side and group closest values.
z-m-06-04.s.s2.hint.1: Your words let reader know how much to trust value?
z-m-06-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You write length so reader no mistake am as 'exactly this much'?
z-m-06-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Your reason come from measuring method or value differences?
z-m-06-04.s.s2.model.0: Hallway length about 3m 40cm. Two marked measurements nearly same: 3m 40cm and 3m 41cm.
z-m-06-04.s.s2.model.1: Hallway length between 3m 40cm and 3m 46cm. We measure three times and answers differ small each time.

z-m-06-06.title: From how many cm we call pencil 'long'?
z-m-06-06.topic: Classification: setting clear criterion with numbers
z-m-06-06.goal: Set clear numeric criterion such as length (cm) for subjective category like 'long pencil'; know same data fit get multiple criteria.
z-m-06-06.material: We measure 8 pencils: 9cm, 11cm, 12cm, 14cm, 15cm, 17cm, 18cm, 20cm. All length measurements whole cm, all different. Jinseo wan divide pencils into 'long' and 'short'. First Jinseo decide 'long pencils look long; short ones look short.'
z-m-06-06.thinking.2: Knowing different criteria fit give same result
z-m-06-06.prereq.0: Reading cm lengths and comparing numbers (Grade 2)
z-m-06-06.s.s1.prompt: Wetin problem with Jinseo first criterion?
z-m-06-06.s.s1.hint.0: Order 8 pencils by length and point where you sure long pencils start.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.hint.1: Think whether you and friend go put middle pencil on same side if you divide separately.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.o.a: Counts of long and short pencils no equal.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.r.a: You confuse dividing rule with group counts. Both groups no need same size.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.o.b: We no measure lengths in cm.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.r.b: Measuring useful, but even with lengths, same problem remain if no decide where 'long' start.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.o.c: Only 8 pencils, so we no fit divide dem.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.r.c: Even few pencils fit divide into two groups. Problem na criterion, no be count.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.r.d: You point out unclear criterion make result depend on who divide.
z-m-06-06.s.s1.explain: 'Look long' fit mean different things to different people. Middle one, like 15cm, fit go either side, so we need criterion wey give same answer for everybody.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.prompt: Set criterion 'pencil long if length c cm or more' so every person get same result. Make long pencils 3 or more and 5 or fewer, and short pencils 3 or more too (c natural number). If different c give same division, count as one. Find 2 c values giving different divisions.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.hint.0: Order pencils by length and draw line so long side get 3 to 5 pencils.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.hint.1: Move line one place each time and count how long-pencil number change.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.ok.c1: c na natural number 1 or more.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c1: Make c natural number at least 1.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c2: Fewer than 3 long pencils. Try lower criterion.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.ok.c3: Long pencils no more than 5, so short pencils at least 3 too.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.fail.c3: More than 5 long pencils. Raise criterion so short pencils at least 3.
z-m-06-06.s.s2.explain: If c=13 or 14, pencils 14, 15, 17, 18, 20 are long (5). If c=15, 4 pencils at least 15cm; if c=16 or 17, 3 pencils at least 17cm. Every c from 13 to 17 possible, but there are 3 different divisions.
z-m-06-06.s.s3.prompt: Say one advantage of your criterion over Jinseo first ('pencils that look long').
z-m-06-06.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine how people differ about 15cm pencil with Jinseo first rule.
z-m-06-06.s.s3.hint.1: With your rule, check whether 15cm pencil always go same group regardless who divides.
z-m-06-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: With number you set, can you tell right away which group 15cm pencil enter?
z-m-06-06.s.s3.selfAssess.1: If friend use your rule, same result come?
z-m-06-06.s.s3.model.0: If you set 14cm or more, everybody get same result. If decide by eye, people fit divide differently.
z-m-06-06.s.s3.model.1: With number criterion, nobody confused whether 15cm pencil long or short; e clear.

z-m-06-07.title: Can we describe our class from results of asking kids on playground?
z-m-06-07.topic: Survey: who you ask and survey results
z-m-06-07.goal: When reading survey results, learn say number of people and who dem be both matter; revise judgment and confidence with new info.
z-m-06-07.material: We survey 24 students in Class 3 about one favorite sport. Choices soccer, dodgeball, jump rope; each pick one. Hangyeol ask 12 friends met on playground during break.
z-m-06-07.thinking.0: Separating surveyed group from whole class
z-m-06-07.thinking.1: Change judgment and confidence with new information
z-m-06-07.prereq.0: Sort data, count and compare more and less (Grade 2 level)
z-m-06-07.s.s1.prompt: Each time survey result and new news arrive, choose the judgment wey you fit make now.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.hint.0: Look whether the people wey dem survey all be friends for the same place doing the same thing.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.hint.1: Think separately whether new facts change the numbers for result or change how much you trust am.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.info: The result of Hangyeol asking 12 people na soccer 9, dodgeball 2 and skipping rope 1.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin you think now about the sport wey the 24 students for Class 3 like pass?
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.after: Among the 12, soccer get most. But we still no know how the other 12 choose. So e too early to decide for the whole class.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Soccer get most. 9 out of 12 choose am, so the whole class go be the same.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You directly apply the result from the 12 wey dem ask to the whole class. We still no know about the other 12.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Among the 12 wey dem ask, soccer get most. For the whole class, we need know about the rest too.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You talk separately about the people wey dem survey and the whole class.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Na only 12 people, so nothing fit be said.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.r.c: The result from the 12 wey dem survey still be useful evidence. You fit talk as much as the information allow.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Soccer seem to dey ahead, but we no know about the other 12, so I go keep am as guess and find out more.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Na idea to guess with the current result, no be to sure, and try find out more.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.info: Remembering where Hangyeol ask, all 12 be friends playing soccer for playground. Nobody ask the friends for classroom.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.ask: Wen you know this, wetin happen to your first judgment?
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.after: If you ask friends wey dey play soccer, many of them likely to choose soccer. So e harder to trust am as result for whole class. E okay to reduce your confidence, and e okay to ask more friends for classroom too.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.o.a: My first judgment remain the same. 9 people choose am, so soccer get most.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You no check how the new fact affect your judgment.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.o.b: I still think say soccer get most, but I no trust am as much again.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You no change your idea, but you change how much you trust am.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.o.c: E ask as many as 12 people, so where e ask no matter.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You only look how many people and miss who e ask.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.o.d: E ask only friends wey dey play soccer, so throw away this result.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.r.d: You even throw away the point say this result tell wetin those 12 people think.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.o.e: The first result alone make am hard to talk for the whole class, so we suppose ask the friends wey dey classroom too.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.1.r.e: You find who no enter the survey.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.info: Next day, Hangyeol ask all 24 (including the first 12). Result na soccer 10, dodgeball 8 and skipping rope 6.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.after: This time dem survey the whole class, so we fit talk say soccer 10, dodgeball 8 and skipping rope 6. Among the first 12, soccer na 9, but all together e na 10, so only 1 of the 12 wey no dey playground choose soccer. Even though soccer come out again as result, we no for know am from the first survey alone.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.o.a: For result of surveying all 24, soccer get most.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You read the result of the whole class survey.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.o.b: The first survey correct. Na the same soccer, so where e ask no matter.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You think say the first survey method reliable because the result turn out the same.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.o.c: Friends wey choose soccer pass half of the 24.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Half of 24 na 12. Check whether 10 pass half.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Among the first 12, e na 9, but all together na only 10, so only 1 of the 12 wey no dey playground choose soccer.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.st.2.r.d: You compare first survey result with the new one and work out wetin the friends wey dem leave out think.
z-m-06-07.s.s1.reflect: At first, from result of 12, we fit only 'guess'. Wen we learn who e ask, our confidence reduce even though result same. Even though final result come out the same way (soccer) as at first, e no change say the first survey alone no fit show am.
z-m-06-07.s.s2.prompt: Write who and how Hangyeol suppose ask next time e do survey, together with the reason.
z-m-06-07.s.s2.hint.0: Remember where the friends wey dem leave out from first survey dey.
z-m-06-07.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether the method wey you choose collect only friends wey easy to choose one sport.
z-m-06-07.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Na method wey collect friends wey resemble the whole class?
z-m-06-07.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You check say your method no collect only friends wey like one sport?
z-m-06-07.s.s2.model.0: I suppose ask all 24 classmates. If I ask only friends for playground, dem go easily choose soccer and the result go lean one side.
z-m-06-07.s.s2.model.1: I go ask friends for different places equally, like classroom, playground and corridor. That way I no go gather only friends wey like one sport.
z-m-06-07.s.s2.model.2: If you give questionnaire to the whole class, you fit find out wetin every friend think.

z-m-06-09.title: We fit decide Thursday from the table records for three days?
z-m-06-09.topic: Record table: guess the next value from earlier records
z-m-06-09.goal: Know say only the first few values for a record table no fit decide the next one, and correct Doyun word 'must'.
z-m-06-09.material: We measure height of sprout every morning and write am for table. Monday 1cm, Tuesday 2cm, Wednesday 4cm. Thursday record never dey. Doyun talk, 'Increase na 1 and 2, so next e go increase by 3, so Thursday go be 7cm,' and Harin talk, 'Every day e double from day before, so Thursday go be 8cm.'
z-m-06-09.thinking.0: Know say different rules fit match the same data
z-m-06-09.prereq.0: Read table and compare number sizes (Grade 2 level)
z-m-06-09.s.s1.prompt: With only the records for three days in table, we fit decide whose statement correct?
z-m-06-09.s.s1.hint.0: Use Doyun rule make the values from Monday to Wednesday, then compare them with table.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.hint.1: Do the same with Harin rule and put the two results side by side.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.o.a: Harin correct. Rule of doubling simpler.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.r.a: You talk say e correct just because the rule simple. Simple rule no always correct.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.o.b: We no fit decide. Both rules match the records.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.r.b: You try each rule on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday records and notice say both match.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.o.c: Doyun correct. E talk am by working out the amount of increase.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.r.c: You only check whether Doyun rule match Monday to Wednesday records. You no check whether Harin rule match too.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.o.d: Both wrong. We no fit predict sprouts.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.r.d: From the fact say predictions fit be wrong, you jump to say all predictions no use.
z-m-06-09.s.s1.explain: Doyun rule continue as 1, 2, 4, 7, and Harin rule continue as 1, 2, 4, 8. Both rules fit the table from Monday to Wednesday. So with only these three boxes, we no fit decide whose statement correct.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.prompt: Read the lines Doyun talk after that one by one and choose the line wey e claim without evidence.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.hint.0: Give each line name: whether na record so far, guess or conclusion.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.hint.1: Tell the difference between value wey already dey for table as record and value wey I write ahead of time.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.line.1: The increases na 1 and 2, so next e seem say e go increase by 3.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.line.2: Then Thursday na 4 plus 3, so e become 7cm.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.line.3: I write 7cm for table, so Thursday must be 7cm.
z-m-06-09.s.s2.explain: Line 4 na the claim wey e make without evidence. Line 2 talk 'e seem' as guess, and line 3 na calculation say e go be 7 if that guess correct. But for line 4, dem change the guess into 'must'. If you choose line 3, check say the calculation give 7 only if the guess correct.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.prompt: Write wetin you go tell Doyun, wey talk say 'Thursday must be 7cm' before Thursday record show. Put at least one number from table inside.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.hint.0: Put Doyun statement and Harin statement side by side and write wetin same and wetin different.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.hint.1: Think wetin Doyun suppose check before e talk 'must'.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You separately talk which part of Doyun statement correct and which part go too far?
z-m-06-09.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You include say value fit different because another rule dey?
z-m-06-09.s.s3.model.0: E fit be 7cm, but if e double like Harin talk, na 8cm. If we only look 1, 2, 4, we still no fit talk 'must'.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.model.1: We go know only if we measure Thursday. Just because increases na 1 and 2 no make am certain say next na 3.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.model.2: From Monday 1, Tuesday 2, Wednesday 4, I no know whether next na 7 or 8. Make we look Thursday record before we talk.
z-m-06-09.s.s3.model.3: We no know say the one after 4 go be 7. As Harin talk, 8 fit happen too.

z-m-06-10.title: Which group read more books?
z-m-06-10.topic: Compare data: the whole group and one person's share
z-m-06-10.goal: When you compare two groups wey get different number of people, know say total books for group and number of books one person read dey tell different things, then make your own case where the two comparisons give different results.
z-m-06-10.material: We survey number of books two groups for our class read this month. Group 가 get 3 people and Group 나 get 8 people. Everybody for Group 가 read the same number of books, and everybody for Group 나 too read the same number. Total number of books for group na the number one person read, added as many times as the number of people. Somi talk, 'Group 나 get more people, so na Group 나 read more books,' and Jihu talk, 'If you look one person at a time, one Group 가 friend fit don read more.'
z-m-06-10.thinking.0: Tell which things dem dey compare apart
z-m-06-10.thinking.1: Make cases wey give different result yourself
z-m-06-10.thinking.2: Tell two stories from the same data
z-m-06-10.prereq.0: Calculate up to two-digit numbers and compare number sizes (Grade 2 level)
z-m-06-10.s.s1.prompt: How we fit look at wetin Somi and Jihu talk?
z-m-06-10.s.s1.hint.0: For one sentence, talk 'the number of wetin' Somi and Jihu dey each compare.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.hint.1: Decide how many books one person read, add am as many times as people dey for the group, then write total books for group.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.o.a: Na only Somi correct. Group wey get more people go also read more books.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.r.a: You think say if people plenty, books go always plenty. You no check how many books one person read.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.o.b: The two statements dey compare different things. Whole group and one person different.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.r.b: You point out say total number of books for group and number of books one person read na different comparisons.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.o.c: Na only Jihu correct. Number of people no get anything to do with number of books.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.r.c: You miss say number of people affect total number of books for group.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.o.d: Both wrong. If you no know how many books dem read, you no fit compare.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.r.d: If you no know book count, you no fit give exact number, but you fit say which cases possible.
z-m-06-10.s.s1.explain: Somi talk total books whole group read, Jihu talk books one person read. Even if group with more people read more together, one by one the smaller group fit have read more.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.prompt: In Group 가, each person read g books; in Group 나 each read h (g and h natural numbers 1 to 9). Make 2 different (g,h) where both Somi and Jihu statements true: ① As group, 나 read more than 가. ② Per person, 가 friend read more than 나 friend.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.hint.0: Choose per-person book counts so 가 higher than 나, then find each group's total and compare.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.hint.1: If 나 no lead in total, think which side number to change.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.var.g: Books read by one person in Group 가
z-m-06-10.s.s2.var.h: Books read by one person in Group 나
z-m-06-10.s.s2.ok.c1: Both numbers natural numbers from 1 to 9.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.fail.c1: Make g and h natural numbers from 1 to 9.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.ok.c2: As whole group, Group 나 read more.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.fail.c2: Group 나 must get more as whole. Group 가 get 3 people and Group 나 get 8.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.ok.c3: Per person, Group 가 read more.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.fail.c3: Per person, Group 가 must read more than Group 나.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.explain: For example, if each 가 person read 4 books and each 나 person 3, 가 total 4 books each for 3 people; 나 total 3 each for 8. So 나 read more as group, but each 가 person read more.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.because.prompt: Write what Somi and Jihu each compare and why both statements fit be true.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.because.hint.0: For your example, write total books in Group 가 and Group 나.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.because.hint.1: For same example, compare which group get more books per person.
z-m-06-10.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You separate which number Somi and Jihu talk about?

z-m-06-11.title: Which list of choices good for survey about how students come to school?
z-m-06-11.topic: Survey: overlaps and gaps when making choice list
z-m-06-11.goal: Learn say survey choices must not overlap and must handle missing cases so each friend mark exactly one; find and fix choice-list problems.
z-m-06-11.material: Grade 2 Class 3 survey 'how you come to school.' Each person mark only way they use most. Three lists: (가) walk, bus, subway, other ways; (나) walk, bus, subway, bicycle, car; (다) walk, vehicle, bus, bicycle. We don't know ways class friends use; some may ride scooter or village bus.
z-m-06-11.thinking.1: Finding way to handle missing cases
z-m-06-11.s.s1.prompt: Which choice list let every person choose one and mark exactly one box?
z-m-06-11.s.s1.hint.0: For each list, check if friend arriving by kick scooter get a box.
z-m-06-11.s.s1.hint.1: For each list, count whether one person fit have one box or at least two boxes.
z-m-06-11.s.s1.r.a: You miss say bus and bicycle included in vehicle, so one person fit fit two boxes.
z-m-06-11.s.s1.r.b: You notice cells no overlap and omitted travel mode fit go under 'other ways.'
z-m-06-11.s.s1.r.c: These five no overlap. But think where scooter or village-bus friend go mark.
z-m-06-11.s.s1.r.d: You no check whether lists have overlaps or gaps.
z-m-06-11.s.s1.explain: (가) no overlap and anyone fit mark a box. (나) works only if you already know class use only these five ways. (다) vehicle overlaps bus and bicycle, so one person fit use two boxes.
z-m-06-11.s.s2.prompt: Give one example how friend wey get trouble with (다) come to school, then say how to fix (다).
z-m-06-11.s.s2.hint.0: Find a case in (다) where same friend fit mark two boxes.
z-m-06-11.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether that friend fit mark just one with fixed list.
z-m-06-11.s.s2.selfAssess.0: With your example, did you show one person fits two boxes?
z-m-06-11.s.s2.model.0: Bus rider fit mark both 'vehicle' and 'bus,' confusing. 'Vehicle' include bus and bicycle, so remove one of those.
z-m-06-11.s.s2.model.1: Bicycle rider fit mark both vehicle and bicycle, overlapping. Remove 'vehicle' and add 'other ways.'
z-m-06-11.s.s2.model.2: Bus rider fit mark vehicle and bus. Remove vehicle and make boxes for subway and car.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.prompt: We use (가), and 'other ways' get most. What should we do before announcing result?
z-m-06-11.s.s3.hint.0: Think what information missing because many answer 'other ways.'
z-m-06-11.s.s3.hint.1: Write which friends need another survey and how to use results already collected.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.o.a: Announce result as is, saying other ways was most.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.r.a: You announce without knowing what 'other ways' include. Readers may not understand.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.o.b: Erase other ways and compare only remaining boxes.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.r.b: You remove box with most answers, losing biggest part of survey.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.o.c: Ask those friends which ways they use and divide answers again.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.r.c: This method break down 'other ways' to find common travel modes.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.o.d: Repeat whole survey from beginning and announce again.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.r.d: You throw away all collected results. Think whether only other-ways group need follow-up.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.explain: If other ways most, find which modes common inside. Ask only people in that box and divide their answers; you keep useful results already collected.
z-m-06-11.s.s3.acc.0: Redoing whole survey works too, but better use results we have and investigate only missing part.
